newsitem.title: UK: P&I insurers to reduce reinsurance - HSBC Gibbs.
newsitem.headline: P&I insurers to reduce reinsurance - HSBC Gibbs.

text.p: Protection & Indemnity (P&I) insurers will reduce their dependence on commercial reinsurers, insurance broker HSBC Gibbs said in its 1996 review of the P&I sector.

"It is likely that the level of club retention will continue to increase," the HSBC subsidiary said, noting that one P&I club has said it would like to see club retention for a single accident rise to $10 million from $5.0 million.
A difference of opinion on the issue of retention could lead to a split in the International Group, which comprises 14 mutual marine liability insurers, known as P&I clubs, HSBC Gibbs said.
"If this is the case, then maybe two groups will appear -- one offering a low limit and one offering a higher limit," it added.
However, in the current soft market, with reinsurance readily available, HSBC said that a large increase in retention levels was unlikely in the short term.
The broker also called on P&I clubs to disclose estimates of Incurred But Not Reported (IBNR) losses.
"This estimate is essential to allow a potential member to accurately consider the underlying security of the club," HSBC Gibbs director Ian Harris director said in a statement.
The HSBC Gibbs review looks at 16 clubs and London based Osprey Underwriting Agency Limited.
